title: Per-turn latency prism and alert resonance controller
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Adds a new per-turn latency visualization ("prism") in the Console and an alert resonance controller which reduces noisy SLO alerts by correlating per-turn latency spikes with token-cost and kernel-queue metrics.
description:
Context and motivation:
We frequently surface noisy latency alerts that are dominated by multi-turn conversational tails. Existing per-invocation metrics conflate turn boundaries and hide internal turn-level latency/cost patterns. This PR adds two pieces: 1) a per-turn latency "prism" visualization that slices traces and aggregated metrics by conversational turn (start/end token anchors), and 2) an alert resonance controller service that reduces false-positive SLO alerts by correlating short-lived per-turn bursts with kernel-queue and prefetch warmup signals before escalating.

What this changes (high level):
- Console: new UI panel 'Per-turn Latency Prism' under Observability -> Invocations with selectable aggregation windows (p50/p95/p99) and turn-length heatmap overlays.
- Telemetry: new metric invocation.turn.p95_latency_ms and turn.token_cost_estimate (derived at ingestion time using existing per-token cost model).
- Alerting: a new controller (obs/alert-resonance) which evaluates candidate alerts and performs a lightweight resonance check across three signals: per-turn latency spike, kernel_queue_depth, and prefetch_warmup_ratio. If the resonance score is below threshold, the alert is attenuated (auto-silenced for 5m) and annotated for later review.
- Ingestion pipeline: small enrichment step that tags invocation traces with turn anchors (token offsets) when present. This is opportunistic and falls back gracefully when anchors are missing.

Small code excerpt (turn anchor tagging):

if let Some(anchor_tokens) = extract_turn_anchors(&trace) {
    trace.tags.insert("turn_anchors", anchor_tokens.join(","));
}

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for extractor and resonance scoring included in the PR.
- Smoke tests run in CI exercise the Console panel via headless browser and verify p95 numbers agree with instrumentation for synthetic multi-turn invocations.
- Canary rollout: feature is behind a flag; we enabled it for 12 internal tenants for 48 hours and validated that alert volume on the test SLO decreased by ~22% without missing true positives during manual fault injection.

Operational notes / roll out plan:
1) Merge to main with feature flag OFF.
2) Stage rollout to internal tenants (feature flag -> 12 tenants) for 48h; monitor invocation.prism.query_time_ms and resonance.attenuation_count.
3) If attenuation_count / total_alerts > 0.15 but false-positive triage remains low, increase tenant set.
4) After 2 weeks and runbook updates, enable for GA.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- Turn enrichment is best-effort; when anchors are absent, ingestion and existing metrics behave as before.
- Resonance controller is throttled and annotates every suppressed alert for manual review; requires operator opt-in.

[Reply by Sofia Patel on 2026-02-20]: "Both addressed: per-tenant thresholds added to controller config (services/obs/controller/resonance/config.rs) and a suppressed_alert_validation metric exported to observations.metrics. I've also added docs in runbook describing how to tune thresholds per tenant."

[Comment by Maya Gonzalez on 2026-02-21]: "Console looks good, but the heatmap color scale needs a fixed legend; otherwise users misinterpret p50 vs p99 bands."
[Reply by Sofia Patel on 2026-02-21]: "Updated the UI to include a fixed legend, added a toggle for normalized vs absolute scales. See commit c4d998e."

[Approval by Liam O'Connor on 2026-02-23]: "Approved after verifying unit tests and canary numbers. CI green."

Why this is unique / impact:
- The per-turn prism lets SREs and engineers see internal conversational structure that was previously buried in invocation-level aggregates; this is especially valuable for chat apps with varying turn lengths.
- Resonance controller addresses alert noise by correlating orthogonal signals (kernel queue and prefetch warmup) rather than relying on single-signal heuristics; in canary we observed a 22% reduction in noisy SLO alerts for multi-turn workloads, improving on-call burden without sacrificing signal fidelity.

Follow-ups (tracked tickets):
- ENG-10111: GA console accessibility fixes and e2e flakiness.
- ENG-10202: Extend resonance checks to consider model-variant fallbacks and cross-region routing events.

If reviewers want, I can split the Console UI into a separate PR to make the telemetry/controller changes land earlier (rollback path would be easier).
